coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: 25B
record.summary: UCSF's June 2025 presentation to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee lists Block 25B, with a use of research, among the undeveloped parcels remaining under its Long Range Development Plan; the same presentation says UCSF has no building plans at Mission Bay right now.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- idealized rectangle (drawn by Pier & Point as a clean rectangle, not a hand trace of the lot's own painted edges) anchored on real street-corner intersections and the real, already-tracked Mission Hall footprint. The lot itself is real (visible painted parking stalls and parked cars in USDA NAIP imagery, viewed 2026-09-29, and in Esri satellite imagery viewed earlier; imagery observations, not stated by the cited UCSF CAC deck); the exact boundary is idealized to a clean rectangle rather than traced to the pavement's own edges.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the Mission Hall/Byers Hall area, as seen in satellite imagery, anchored on the real 4th St x 16th St and 3rd St x 16th St street-corner intersections (earlier attempts using building bounding boxes had repeatedly mis-centered on the wrong block). The resulting open area (about 7,505 sq m before shaping) spans the whole plan block from Mission Hall's own footprint east toward 3rd St; Pier & Point reads it as 25A and 25B combined, with Mission Hall itself being 25A and this record -- the part east of Mission Hall, idealized as a clean rectangle -- being 25B. Chosen and shaped by hand, not taken from a surveyed parcel.

facts.value: Research (UCSF Long Range Development Plan use for Block 25B, slide 3 of the June 2025 presentation)

milestones.text: OCII's Mission Bay Land Use Map (December 2019) splits this block into 25A/25B and shows 25B in the 'UCSF' color; the Successor Agency's Dec 2015 property map (LRPMP Attachment B, page 12) shows block 25 as a single unoutlined block, outside the Park/Affordable-Housing parcel set

changes.text: Added a sourced dossier for Mission Bay South Block 25B.
A map citation on this block no longer gives a date that belongs to the next page of the same document.

Block 25B's notes said the block is a surface parking lot next to the 'Global Health & Clinical Sciences Building'; the cited UCSF June 2025 deck supports only its position, its undeveloped status and its Research designation. The parking lot is now attributed to USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29), the unsourced building alias was removed, and the 2019 milestone now cites the December 2015 property management plan map for the undivided block.

open_questions: No project, developer, architect, design or schedule for Block 25B was found in any source read.
That the site is a surface parking lot today (the record's name) rests on this project's imagery checks; no source read says so.
The record status 'planned' reflects a land-use designation in UCSF's long-range plan, not an active project; the slide itself says there are no building plans at Mission Bay right now.
The slide's map label 'Future Research (25B)' is in the slide image; only the slide's text list was read as text.

record.notes: OCII plan block 25B, shown by UCSF's own Dec 2024-updated campus map (June 2025 CAC deck) as 'Future Research (25B)' and listed under 'Undeveloped parcels remaining'. Immediately east of Mission Hall (25A), between it and 3rd St, north of 16th St; the position matches the deck's map. The block is a surface parking lot in USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29), an imagery observation the deck does not state. Currently undeveloped/planned per the plan designation.
